text_fidelity_a:
Zero Tolerance 0456, Sinkevich Pocket Knife; 3.25” CPM-20CV Steel Blade, Titanium Handle with Stonewash and Satin Finish, KVT Ball-Bearing Opening, Titanium Frame Lock, Reversible Pocketclip; 6.6 OZ,Silver Not familiar with the PARA Warthog? It is a short, stubby, relatively heavy .45 acp semi auto pistol available in stainless steel.. While it won't win any beauty contests, it has a presence all its own and the intimidation factor it provides is awesome. It's the kind of weapon that when you run out of ammo you can hit your opponent in the face with it for the game winner.

This ZT 0456 has that kind of look to it. It has some (short and stubby) curves but the overall construction is what draws attention to itself. Yes, it is a bit on the (slightly) heavy side, but this knife wasn't designed to be slim and beautiful. It is designed to work, and work hard, taking on any task from cutting to prying that you come up against. How many knives do you have in your collection that can be carried in your pocket, can dispatch any simple cutting jobs with aplomb, and then allow you to pry open a door with it. Most EDC blades don't have the spine for it, much less the overall design and build that would allow even attempting that task.

As I have aged I have learned that a knife should be much more than just a cutting tool. None of my automatic knives can even approach the type of hard work that this Zero Tolerance knife can conquer. The blade is sharp but heavy, the locking mechanism is tight and solid, and the flipper works like butter. People notice it when I pull it from my pocket, not just because it's a knife but because of the attractive and unique design. Everyone wants to know what it is, how much it costs, and where can they "legally" get one. This is one of those places.
text_fidelity_b: Zero Tolerance 0456, Sinkevich Pocket Knife; 3.25” CPM-20CV Steel Blade, Titanium Handle with Stonewash and Satin Finish, KVT Ball-Bearing Opening, Titanium Frame Lock, Reversible Pocketclip; 6.6 OZ,Silver

text_fidelity_a:
MASXODRK Universal Scooter Bag,Waterproof and Stable Handlebar Bag for Scooter/EBike/Motorcycle/Bicycle,Large Capacity&Portable EVA Scooter Accessories Storage Bag for Charger,Repair Tools&Phone I fully admit, we got this MASXODRK Scooter Bag, Large Capacity Waterproof Electric Scooter Storage Bag for our two unknown/lesser known brand eScooters not knowing if we had a chance for it to fit. It is not one of the ones listed on the product page, so... in the end, it has worked out great on both our eScooters, so we are happy to have it.

This MASXODRK Scooter Bag, Large Capacity Waterproof Electric Scooter Storage Bag has two straps at the top to go on the handlebars, two on the back to wrap and hold it to the upright stick of the eScooter. But would there be enough room between/around/next too the break and accelerator? For both of ours, yes. They fit slightly differently, but yes, we got them on there, no problem. The straps on the back - one over the other - holds the bag to the stick perfectly. The top ones come with such a long piece of material, you have various options on length down the front stick - we can actually do it at varying heights and simply wrap the remaining material. The ones on the back are a little more limited, but not so much that we could not also adjust - here it was how tight to make it against the stick, and this varied by how high or low we did the top one. In other words, there is enough material on the top two straps that it allowed us to adjust the placement of the bag on the two different eScooters, and on each eScooter itself, for more overall options.

The bag is a good size. We can get both wallets, a phone or two, keys, all in there. The velcro holds it strong enough. And we are good to go. We do NOT ride in any weather, so no idea how it would handle rain - but we never want to find out. We THINK it would be okay and keep stuff good. There is a solid, type material for the shell, cloth for the edges, all SHOULD hold back the rain - but that cloth COULD potentially get soaked and leaked. But our understanding of eScooters - you'd have a bigger problem with the scooter getting wet first.

In the end we are thrilled with this MASXODRK Scooter Bag, Large Capacity Waterproof Electric Scooter Storage Bag and while we are using it on our eScooters, we feel it would go on a bike or other item as well, depending on the design of course, but opens more options for using it. We're thrilled.
text_fidelity_b: MASXODRK Universal Scooter Bag,Waterproof and Stable Handlebar Bag for Scooter/EBike/Motorcycle/Bicycle,Large Capacity&Portable EVA Scooter Accessories Storage Bag for Charger,Repair Tools&Phone

This set is so convenient for her because it contains the smaller towel to wipe sweat off while playing as well as the bath towel to use when she showers off after the game.

She's 5'9 and has long hair, so she said the towel wraps around her nicely, and once she's dressed she wrings it out then uses it to wrap her hair as well to dry it faster. They don't take up much space whatsoever so she just tucks them into her backpack again and heads back to the next class.

We like to go camping, swimming in the river near us, and kayaking, so I think each of us will have a set of these for our future trips because they'll take up a lot less space in our dry bags than regular towels and dry faster too. I received mine at a discounted cost for evaluation and review purposes, but they're so convenient to have both of these sizes that I'm buying more at full price. Besides the gym and camping trips, these would be convenient for a kid who plays sports in school, or for traveling too. Just be sure to remember the way to use these is to blot yourself dry rather than rub yourself down like you would with a regular towel. They took turns for the next hour or so. Before this, I had my son riding on a towel on my rear rack. He would hold my seat post and most of the time bury his face in my back so that he wouldn't fall off. He also had to hold his legs out so that his feet wouldn't get caught in the chain or the tire. With this seat, he can sit back in comfort, he has his own little handlebars to hold, and the seat is nice and soft for him. He is extremely happy that I got this for him.

Installation was a little difficult, but nothing crazy. I would have loved a second pair of hands to help me install, but the rest of my family was suddenly busy when I started putting it on. The only part that was hard was getting the crossbar on under the rack. One of the support beams would be right next to the bar, no matter how I installed the seat. It took a little maneuvering, but I managed to wedge the crossbar in and get the seat bolted down. Even if a nut falls off, I don't think the seat will move because of the way it is wedged on. So I feel it's very safe. One thing I wouldn't mind is having the brace that holds the backrest be a little more sturdy.

It's been a few weeks now and so far everything has held up. The bike was left out in the rain a few times, but I don't notice any rust appearing. I'm pretty pleased with this purchase.

Electric Battery Operated Heated Socks Men Women Rechargeable Washable for Hunting Winter Skiing Mobile Warming Powered Battery Heated Socks… I had high hopes for these electric socks. I mean, electric blankets have been around forever, right? So maybe, just maybe these would work. Sadly, they are utter crap.

When they arrived, they didn't look too bad. I was concerned about how much of the sock would have a heated area, but I figured, even a relatively small area might be helpful. I got some fresh AA batteries and loaded up the battery compartments. (There is a little pocket near the top outer side of each sock. There is a wire inside each of these that connects to the battery box.)

I felt just the faintest bit of warmth from one sock and nothing from the other. I put them on and honestly could not tell a difference between the non-working side and the one that was faintly warm. I thought perhaps they needed more time to warm up, so I continued wearing them hoping that would happen. I was busy working and after a couple of hours realized that they had never warmed up. So I decided to check the batteries, 'just in case,' they weren't fully charged. When I checked them on my battery tester, all four were completely dead even though I had gotten them from my fresh supply. I wondered if they could possibly have been bad to begin with, though that seemed highly unlikely. Then I wondered if the box had somehow drained the batteries.

Still holding out a tiny bit of hope the socks would warm, I got out more batteries. This time I checked them with my battery tester first, to make sure they were fully charged. They were. Again I felt the tiniest bit of warmth and thought, "Great! I guess the last batch of batteries were no good."

Put them on and again, could not feel the warmth. I later checked the fully charged batteries and .. you guessed it, they were drained. So not only did the stupid socks not work, they somehow drained EIGHT AA batteries!! What a waste of time and money. Needless to say, I want to send these back.

It's really a shame because a lot of people would love to have socks like this if they would actually work. I hope the manufacturer figures out a way to make them work AND do so without having to go through dozens of batteries each week.
text_fidelity_b: Electric Battery Operated Heated Socks Men Women Rechargeable Washable for Hunting Winter Skiing Mobile Warming Powered Battery Heated Socks…

Zumba Fitness Tone Up DVD System New Years resolutions anyone? This boxed set has everything you need to get started on a fitness program. The first thing you notice when you open the kit is the weights. They are shakers. How fun is that? Two booklets are included.One, the program guide, offers a schedule for using the workouts. I don't know about you, but doing the same thing every day bores me. That's not a problem with this set. The program guide suggests using different workout routines every day of the week, with a day of rest after each two days of workouts. The exercise choreography itself is not only sound for building fitness, it's also witty, imaginative, and lots of fun. I'm out of shape, so I have to modify the movements a lot, but the instructors are excellent and work into each movement slowly, pointing out correct form to avoid injury. My room is very small, and some of the dance moves do take a little more space than I have. It's not just standing in one spot, but I am still able to do them. The chair routines are fantastic. They are designed for your upper body and abs, but you really get a full body workout.

Also included is a booklet with a great nutrition guide. It has a full week's worth of meals with recipes, and it's small enough to stick in your purse or pocket when you go to the store. The meals feature the latest weight-loss and cardiac health superstars, but everything you need will be at your neighborhood supermarket.

The heart of the program is a set of four DVDs with the instructions and specialized workouts. There is also a bonus "Fitness Concert" for those of you who are more advanced. It's great to go to a live class, but in the winter that can be hard. There are also advantages to dancing around your own room. (no embarrassment when you trip over your own feet)

I love this! When New years resolutions involve fun, they're more likely to get done.
text_fidelity_b: Zumba Fitness Tone Up DVD System

I will update this further, once ski season starts.

text_fidelity_a:
Franklin Sports Shoot N Score Hockey Shootout Game Great idea, and it is fun! But... Franklin cut so many corners making this, it ruins it.
Problems with the game:
* Shoddy build quality, the parts do not stay together as they should. Annoying to build, and rebuild during play
* No volume control! This thing is loud! but its an indoor toy. A volume control would have made it much more enjoyable.
* No storage for the balls - a little drawer or a cover for the channel that contains them during play would have helped hugely
* Only 30 second games. Why not a range? add one minute, three minutes and five minutes!
* Poor design allows the ball to often get trapped behind the goalie
* Poor design allows the ball to easily get trapped behind the player (and with only 30 seconds to play, these two issues can be real game spoilers)
* Poor design allows you to quite often "score" even though the ball did not score, it bounced of the goalie and jumped the side rail/

If you can put up with all of that, it is a lit of fun. It is such a shame that they did not put just a little more work into it to make it a great game.
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Shoot N Score Hockey Shootout Game

I set it on a smart plug timer so it could even do a late night batch without running all night. I used to do ultrasonic cleaning but I hated the drying process and the less pleasing lack of that brassy shine you get with tumbling.
A couple pieces of advice....I saw reviewers mentioning the center bolt dinging up brass, the fix is SUPER easy. A simple drinking straw to cover the threads. I even found a blue one that matches the tumbler.
Second piece of advice, don't be dumb like me. I had a handful of .223 that I decided to add to the .40 cal I was tumbling. .223 fits in the .40 cal so many of the .223 had unpolished bases. Just remember 9 mm fits in .40 and .40 fits in .45. so pay attention if you mix brass. Make sure it can't fit inside the other type.
text_fidelity_b: Frankford Arsenal Quick-N-EZ 110V Case Tumbler Kit with Sifter for Brass Cartridge Cleaning and Polishing for Reloading

After you’re done using the scope you have to press both the red and green buttons to turn off. You can see in the company’s listed picture how it shows the off button with arrows pointing downward on both red/green buttons.

My final thoughts are this scope is of good value. It is also waterproof and shockproof according to the manual.

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) My first one wouldn't hold a charge for longer than a day and a half, but I was able to rather easily get a refund for that one, and purchase a brand new one.

I use the iPhone app almost exclusively, since the Windows program is inexcusably bad. Theoretically any device with Bluetooth 4.0 should be able to talk to the Charge, but my Android tablet was unable to, so until I got my iPhone I was forced to use the Windows program along with a small USB FitBit dongle.

The Windows program has absolutely no other function then to sync with the Charge, Which in theory you can do anytime that the charge is within range. But my installation of Windows 7 ultimate was unable to perform this task without me specifically launching the program and telling it to sync.

With the exception of doing a little of the initial setup, other than that single function of retrieving information from the Charge, passing it on to the FitBit website and vice-versa, the Windows desktop program does nothing. Literally nothing.

The fact that the desktop app does nothing, forces you forces the users without a FitBit compatible phone or tablet to perform everything that ought to be able to be doable locally on the webpage.

Things like, choosing a watch face, or determining the order in which things are displayed, or determining what, if anything, a double tap on the watch face does.

Some other useful changes I would like to see are:

+ Personally, since the FitBit communicates via Bluetooth, I see no reason why the FitBit Bluetooth dongle that comes with the device can't be used by the computer that you plug it into as a Bluetooth dongle. They just need to write drivers specific to their dongle, which they already have, that have a way of seizing control of the dongle when it needs to transmit, and then return control of the dongle to the regular Bluetooth system when it's done. We've already paid for the Bluetooth dongle, we might as well be able to use it, even if we only ever use the app.

+ Most usefully, change the clock faces to show:
1) Remaining battery charge! (Could just be asterisks, periods, or even the pipe symbol | .)
2) The Day of the Week!
3) The Date! (MM/DD)
4) Option to display AM/PM with 12 hour watch faces.

+ Add the "Connected GPS" that the new Blaze boast's!

+ Of course, change the desktop program so that you can do all the things that you can do on both the website and the apps, on your computer.

+ Changing how the app displays your sleep data so that it includes the amount of time that you slept deeply, or were in interrupted sleep.

+ Making the website more intuitive.
+ Have the website display your sleep data in a useful manner.

+ A larger range of watch faces to choose from, not just the current four.
+ The option of an analog watch face.
+ Add a screen to the charge that displays at least some of your sleep data.
+ Allow the Charge to be accessed via Bluetooth, so that even phones unable to install the fit bit app can still send text and caller and information to it.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in))

Clement Cycling Strada LGG Clincher 120 TPI Tire I recently bought a new Specialized Sirrus hybrid bicycle. Toady I swapped out the OEM tires and tubes for Clement Cycling Strada LGG 120 TPI 700cx28 clincher tires and Continental MTB/Race 28 700x25-32 tubes with 60mm Presta valves. The LGG tires weigh 233g each (my actual measurements), compared to 478g for the stock Espoir Sport Reflect 700x30c tires. The width of the LGG's on the stock 26mm (outside width) rims is 29.8mm, compared to 32.4mm for the stock tires. The Conti tubes weigh 140g, compared to 154g for the stock tubes. The overall weight savings was a surprising 259g, or 9.14oz, for each wheel.

Riding at the same tire pressure, 70 lbs front and 75 lbs back, the LGG tires had much quicker handling and the ride felt more cushioned. The more cushioned ride may be due to the heavy, relatively stiff carcass on the stock tires compared to the very lightweight and flexible sidewalls on the LGGs.

text_fidelity_a: WILSON Pro Staff Team Tennis Racket, 4 3/8", Black/White I play a LOT of tennis and am trying to improve my game through personal, regular lessons, and a lot of team practice and matches.  I play doubles and singles and am very serious about the game.  That said, I'm giving this racquet 5 stars for now.  I've only played with it a couple of times but each time was fairly long.  I played with it today in a friendly singles tennis match against a woman whom I practice with, and is at least a 4.0 player.  So far I like it.  The strings are factory strings and are very tight - very little if any give even when hitting hard.  I will probably get a good set of Prince strings put on it later on.  It's a little heavier than my Head Ti.s6 (very light) and the weight seems to be mainly in the top part of the racquet head.  That's good because  I can get some extra down motion going in my serve thus more power.  It has more power than my Head and I am still learning to keep it under control.  I find my serves are going a little faster and deeper with this racquet than with my Head racquet.  I also use to play with a Prince O3 racquet but found it to be on the heavy side - the Wilson Pro Staff is much lighter.  My singles practice partner wanted to play with it today and she really loved it.  It took her a while to get her serves where she usually places them but after about an hour of playing she was into this racquet.  My coach took a look at this racquet and seemed to like it pretty good but didn't try it out.  This review is from a female perspective and we don't usually hit as hard as men, so the review might not be as useful to you if you're male with a powerful stroke.  The racquet I received for review has a grip size of 4 3/8" and I normally use a  4 1/4, but the 4 3/8 felt fine and I made good, well placed  solid strokes with it. I might even move up to the a 4 3/8" later on.  In conclusion, I think this would be a very good racquet for a man or woman and the price is reasonable (as of this review it costs $139.00).  It's seems to be solid, well-constructed and well balanced (except for maybe the extra weight in the head but that really didn't seem to bother me in the least and it helped my serves.)

text_fidelity_a:
Franklin Sports Arctic Trails Hiking Poles - Lightweight - Anti Shock Technology - Great for All Skill Levels I've had a set of MSR trek poles for over a decade now. I've used them to travel though the Zion river, down and up the grand canyon, through forests of sequoias and so on. They've always worked well, but there's been newer tech since I first bought them.

So I put them side by side for a comparison. Here's how's the two stack up.
They both operate in the same way as far as extending and turning to lock them.
They are both clearly marked so you always knows your set length.
As shown in the photo, the MSRs are a bit taller when extended. They're both just about the same height when collapsed.
The MSRs did not come with option for swappable end caps.
The hand grips on these are softer.
As shown in the other photo, the tip shield on the MSRs are indexed so they interlock. That keeps them from swinging around.
And probably the biggest difference is that these have shock absorption. There's just enough spring to take off some of the abruptness of planting these down on unstable footing without there being too much travel to throw off stability.

So overall, they work well. They're an improvement overt the old ones in some ways. In others, they're not.
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Arctic Trails Hiking Poles - Lightweight - Anti Shock Technology - Great for All Skill Levels

And yes, the package was relatively difficult to open, probably to discourage five-fingered shoppers from stealing them off the shelves. Unfortunately there are no instructions included for those who may not intuitively figure out how to install the batteries and use the three lighting functions (high, low, strobe).

Being short, slippery, and not confidence inspiring as far as using it -- and only having an estimated 2.5 hour battery life -- what is this really good for? The functionality is in its small size and very bright light. This would be an excellent tool for those working in small and dark spaces, casting enough clear and bright light for close detail work. Working under a sink with a Maglite LED 3D Cell Flashlight just doesn't cut it. This Energizer is small enough to prop up against anything in your work area to help focus the beam while freeing both hands for whatever task you're undertaking. The light beam cast by it broadens quickly and the choice of a "high" and "low" setting increase its usefulness. Believe it or not, it can actually be too bright for close work using the "high" beam.

This 250 Lumen Energizer is fine for short operating periods either inside or outside the house. However its very limited battery life restricts it to use as a back-up flashlight. For overall effectiveness as an emergency light source (blackouts, storms, indoor/outdoor security) nothing really beats a Maglite LED Flashlight using 3 D batteries. For $22.72 (compared to $14.99 for this Energizer) you have a 168 lumen light which casts a beam as far as 412 meters and has an eight hour battery life. We have several in our home that are red in color which makes them easier to find in a stressful situation. Not only that, but the Maglites are hefty enough to use as a striking weapon if need be. It's certainly better to have in your hand than nothing at all.
text_fidelity_b: Energizer Vision HD Performance Metal Flashight

text_fidelity_a:
Intex Challenger Kayak, Inflatable Kayak Set with Aluminum Oars and High Output Air-Pump This thing is amazing!! I've taken it out 6 times over the last month, for 2–5 mile jaunts, at local city lakes and sheltered bays, and a couple lakes in a National Park. At this point it's already worth its price: if it failed next outing (I don't think it will) I'd still be happy with it. For less than 100 bucks I have the ability to visit little islands inside lakes, get unbelievable views from the water, and explore wetlands and sloughs that landlubbers can't get to. I can't get over the novelty of launching, docking at some isolated rock beach or island to eat a snack, then coming back over the water. And having the ability to do this where there are no concessionaires almost feels like cheating! The experience is just that amazing. Not to mention ease of transport and storage.

As far as seaworthiness: yes, it tracks poorly even with the skeg but that just means more rotational practice for you. Stable in lake waves and jetski wakes, I've never felt close to capsizing. It's slow. Will blow with the wind if you let it, but you can easily paddle against it. It works, and it'll get you there.

Setup and teardown is easy but it does take some time. The pump is fine and it will inflate faster than you think. For durability: all components feels very heavy and solid, it's like bounce house material. The valves feel strong and actually take some effort to release the air. I take care not to beach the kayak, or set up/tear down on any surface too rocky or spiky. I also take lengths to dry it afterwards: I point fans at it for a few hours, making sure to get the inside crevices dry. I feel optimistic it'll be fine for a while.

Standard hacks: Get a large IKEA blue bag to carry the actual deflated kayak, use the included (flimsy) bag for the other components, pump, your PFD. Don't inflate the seat-bottom for more vertical leg room.

When researching this, I talked to 2 paddling-adventure friends and inflatable kayaks are perfectly respectable and even the choice of some extreme adventurers: see Audrey Sutherland's amazing books and adventures, and look up Grabner inflatables. Enjoy!!!
text_fidelity_b: Intex Challenger Kayak, Inflatable Kayak Set with Aluminum Oars and High Output Air-Pump

High Sierra Packaged Reservoir, White/Black, 3 L This is nothing really, like a camel - back water bottle. You will need a backpack or someway of carrying this reservoir since it does not have straps or anyway to attach to your body like it is. It's made from fairly rugged BPA-free plastic (though still made in China), and when completely full will hold 3 liters. I like the idea of being able to carry 3 liters of water (if necessary) in a backpack and being able to drink it without stopping to get a water bottle from your pack, but it doesn't leave much room for anything else. Also, 3 liters of water is heavy - even 2 liters is a lot to carry over a long trek. Try carrying a 2 liter bottle of soda for a while and you'll get the idea of weight. I know I'll never fill it completely up but will probably only fill about 1/2 up. I like to hike a lot and am anxious to actually take this on a long hike. I've only walked around the neighborhood with it and it did alright except I had to keep the water cord underneath my backpack shoulder strap near my face if I wanted to drink.

The opening at the top is big, very much like the slide clip opening on some older model vacuum cleaners where the bag is held. It comes off and goes back on securely with no problems. I can get my hand down inside the bag to clean it or at least thoroughly rinse it out. Overall, I think it is a good water reservoir, but for me personally, I would go with a 1 or no bigger than a 2 liter. A person with a very strong back and a big thirst will love this one.

Application is very easy -- just peel off the backing tape (the strip has glue on one side), slowly wrap the bat with each wrap overlapping a small amount, and you're done. It also includes a piece of finishing tape (small length of black tape) for the final row to keep things looking tidy. Once applied it's very secure -- the glue is strong.

You do want to take care not to stretch the material too much when applying it. Keep it tight when applying so there's no wrinkles or gaps, but don't stretch it.

The material is thin so it doesn't add much at all to the bat diameter, but the added grip is outstanding. Plus, it makes for a more comfortable grip as well.

I imagine this would be a great grip material to use on any item that would benefit from a more secure grip and/or a more comfortable grip. While it's sized perfectly for bats, use on smaller or larger items is certainly possible since it has an adhesive backing.

text_fidelity_a:
Wenzel Evergreen Tent - 6 Person Update: We returned the original tent and dually had a chance to use the replacement sent and......

Same exact problem. Almost no wind, light rain and the poles bent at a ridiculous angle before snapping. Wenzel is the worst brand of tent I've ever used. Can't return it since it was last season's replacement so we sound up throwing what was left away. I regret not Judy buying a Coleman for the same price when I had the chance.
I'll start out saying that Wenzel in general is a very quality name and usually makes quality products. That being said I was very unhappy with this particular tent. Despite the usual common sense I have when I buy gear I didn't check the package before heading out (entirely my fault there). It's a good thing I keep a just in case kit in our vehicle because there were no pegs at all in the package, not even the little peg bag (and yes, It was bought new and still in the package as well as the Amazon box). No big deal there, just a minor annoyance.

I set the tent up with help of another avid camper friend of mine who's had this same exact tent for about a year and uses it like crazy. About two hours later a small sprinkling rain came up with some soft wind. His kids were enjoying tent time and listening to the rain when suddenly one of the poles splintered very quickly and sliced open my arm a few inches. suffice to say it was a very bad day and there were a several spooked and unhappy children as their dad had to take us all through the backwoods to a clinic so I could get stitches. Not the best birthday party a kid can have. I have had a couple of tents splinter their poles before but it's never been so violent nor had such a brittle quality to it. They've looked more like shreds while this just broke off in several jagged pieces and a few very sharp splinters left behind.

This is not the usual Wenzel quality and I'm hoping it's just a fluke. Perhaps it's the design? A badly handled or worn out pole? I don't know. But be aware that this might be a problem. Going through one of the many reviews I did find one where a woman had a pole splinter suddenly and go in to her hand. I wish I'd found that review before buying. I'm returning this one to Amazon for replacement in hopes that it was just one of those random things and will update if it happens again.
text_fidelity_b: Wenzel Evergreen Tent - 6 Person

The scooter in general is great and able to take me from point A to point B in a timely manner. One feature that really makes the scooter user friendly is the battery. Being able to take the battery out and leave the scooter outside while charging it inside is extremely convenient.

The keys that come with the scooter are also extremely convenient. With the NFC feature it’s easy to unlock, all you have to do is touch the key to the scooter’s digital interface.

Making sure you have enough battery is important if you are planning on going somewhere far. The gauge on the scooter doesn’t give you an accurate idea of how far you can go, and the apps percentages aren’t very accurate either.

One other thing I wish it had was a longer pole. It is tall enough for my hand to reach it when I’m standing but it has to be fully extended so it can be awkward and unsafe. If it was a little bit longer, it’d be perfect for sitting and standing.

It is most comfortable to ride while sitting but you are able to stand. Depending on your height, standing may feel comfortable or a bit awkward. If you’re around the 6ft range it feels slightly too short to use while standing, although it is possible. It would've been nice if some adjustments have been made in the scooter so that it would have been easy to use both sitting and standing.

The scooter is really easy to operate. Right out of the box, all you do is turn it on and go. The acceleration is quick and the brakes are fast and efficient.

The scooter is made in China and being sold by Chinese company on Amazon. At the current price of 700 bucks I'm sure it's at least 250 bucks over priced.
text_fidelity_b: OKAI EA10 Electric Scooter with Seat, Up to 25-35 Miles Range & 15.5MPH, Moped Scooter Bike for Adults with 10 Inch Vacuum Tires

This one was much cheaper and I wanted one that used AC to charge or to run.  My other pump connected to the car battery.  Once of the issues for me is that I am often inflating my raft or water toy while it is on the trailer.  So, the pump needs to run off its own power or I need a cable that is long enough to reach the battery or cigarette lighter.  This pump can be charged with AC then you can take it anywhere to use.  I tested it on an SUP and it did fine on its own battery.  The listing says it can be used for 1 hour which is more than enough time to pump up a raft, kayak and an SUP.  It has + and - buttons to set the air pressure you want to achieve.  The main problem I had was none of the connectors would fit my SUP valve.  One of them looked like it should fit but wouldn't stay connected.  So I tested it adding air while holding the hose in place and it did fine.  I tried doing the same with deflation and could not get it to deflate.  It seemed there was a slight vacuum that could be felt but it was not enough to work without having a tight connection.  I am giving it the benefit of the doubt by only reducing the stars to 4.  Otherwise it is a strong hefty unit that comes in a bag that also holds the AC cord and hose with various connectors.

I still use my combination cable lock to lock my trunk pack and wheel. I put this U-lock around the bike rack and bike frame and use it to lock my helmet, too. text_fidelity_a:
SUBOOS Compact 3-in-1 Rechargeable LED Camping Lantern and Flashlight - 290 Lumens, Waterproof, Great for Suvival Kit, Emergency, Hurricane, Power Outage. We sometimes have seasons of power outages where I live. That is not a problem sometimes, but if it is a long extended one, it is handy to have lights available to use so we can continue life as normal as much as possible, especially in unlit areas like bathroom and basement. Let's take a look.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This light is quite compact, yet large enough to stand up on the table. It has a hanging wire on the top of it that folds down. There is a round cloudy covering on the bottom, and a clear reflective opening on the top for the flashlight. There are curved textured see through coverings which are for red lights either constant or flashing.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
This is really quite handy. A quick press will turn on the basic light. Another press, medium. Another press, high. One more press. Off. The light is pretty easy to see with and makes a great light if you have to work hands free at a table, or near metal surface which it will magnetically stick to.

FLASHLIGHT
The flashlight has two rapid presses and then one more will turn it brighter then off.

RED LIGHT
If you need to use a red light or need to attract attention you can use the red light consistent or flashing.

BOOKLET
The booklet in the package is well written and has great instructions how to use this.

CHARGING
The charging cord is USB to mini USB cord. There are five blue lights on the side and they will light up as the light is charged. When done, they stay lit until you unplug it.

LONGEVITY
We got several hours out of this on medium and high and it still has half a charge. It charges up pretty quickly in only a couple of hours, and you can use this with a power bank if you need to.

THE BOTTOM LINE

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is a great light to have handy, but over time, if anything changes, I will update. For now, it is performing well and lasts a good amount of time prior to needing a recharge.

text_fidelity_a:
NCAA Kentucky Wildcats Can Cooler, 16 I have this exact same cooler from another team, and got this one as a gift for my cousin, who is a huge fan. This cooler is incredibly well-made and I'm thrilled that I got it! (I ended up buying everyone their favorite team's cooler in this same brand, and they were a huge hit over the holidays!)

The first great surprise when it arrived was that it is made by Coleman, with tags on it to prove it. Coleman doesn't make bad stuff, in fact, they have a long history of well-made products, so that was a really nice bonus.

On top of that, there are all kinds of quality extras built into it. For example, when you lift the lid, there is a mesh ice-pack holder built right into the top of it. On the outside of it, there are mesh holders on each side (I use them for napkins, straws, or nutrition bars). Then in the front there is a nice zippered compartment that you can securely stash a few things in. The zippers are high quality and the materials, inside and out, are high quality as well. The strap is wide, strong and adjustable. Another nice perk is that it has a little pad where the strap will go over the shoulder, which really makes carrying it much more comfortable. The cooler holds a lot, and really does a great job at keeping things nice and cold. I just put my ice packs in it with our bottles, sandwiches, etc., and we are good to go.

I also got one of these coolers for a friend who is disabled and likes to keep a cooler next to her bed. Well, she'd gotten fed up with coolers that didn't keep things cold for very long and she had switched to using a spaghetti pot (for real!) with ice packs in it, to keep her ginger ale chilled, for constant nausea. She said that with a few frozen ice packs in it, she actually can go two whole days without having to replace the ice packs. She also said it fits great on her scooter when she's on the go.

Made by Coleman, like I said, and with lots of nice features, this high quality cooler is a must-have and a great gift. Check out the same cooler with other team logos. Just make sure you get the one like this one from "TLG8," to get the high quality one I just described. Thanks for reading my review. Hope it helped someone.
text_fidelity_b: NCAA Kentucky Wildcats Can Cooler, 16

Caveats: My smartphone, which is about 5 7/8" (~15mm) long, fits nicely in its sleeve, but you won't fit something too much longer in there. -Maybe- another .5".

The material feels a -little- soft. Not enough to be worrisome for my purposes, but if you are more rough-and-tumble and have a lot of sharp/pokey/hard objects or tools, you may have a problem. If you are just throwing this in your beach bag to protect things, though, you should be fine.

Would recommend.
